# list

```go
import "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
```

Package list streams the contents of a vfs.Location as vfs.Entry values, identically on every backend.

### Options

Listings are configured with options, each of which implements options.ListOption:

- [Prefix](<#Prefix>), [Glob](<#Glob>), [Match](<#Match>), [Filter](<#Filter>) and [FilterContext](<#FilterContext>) restrict which entries are yielded.
- [Recursive](<#Recursive>), [MaxDepth](<#MaxDepth>), [DirFilter](<#DirFilter>) and [DirFilterContext](<#DirFilterContext>) control descent into subdirectories.
- [FilesOnly](<#FilesOnly>) and [DirsOnly](<#DirsOnly>) restrict the kind of entry.
- [StartAfter](<#StartAfter>), [After](<#After>) and [Limit](<#Limit>) page through a listing.

Each option may be given at most once, so a caller that adds default options of its own must not repeat them. Invalid combinations are rejected by [ParseQuery](<#ParseQuery>) with an error matching [ErrInvalidOption](<#ErrInvalidOption>) before any request is made. Options that this package does not define, such as backend\-specific options, are ignored.

### Ordering

Entries are yielded in ascending byte order of their order key \(see [OrderKey](<#OrderKey>)\): the entry's relative path, with a trailing "/" for directories. The same order holds on every backend, which makes [StartAfter](<#StartAfter>) a portable cursor.

### Backend implementers

A backend that lists natively implements vfs.EntryLister and starts from [ParseQuery](<#ParseQuery>). The hints in [Query](<#Query>) let it avoid fetching entries that would be discarded, and [Query.Depth](<#Query.Depth>) gives the deepest level it needs to read. Ignoring a hint is never a correctness bug, because the listing applies every option again to what a backend yields.

<a name="After"></a>
## func After

```go
func After(e vfs.Entry) options.ListOption
```

After yields only entries that sort after e, which is the cursor for the next page of a paged listing. It is StartAfter with the order key of e. After cannot be combined with [StartAfter](<#StartAfter>).

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Limit and After page through a listing. The cursor is the last entry of the previous page, so no page needs to remember anything but that entry.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/mem"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/options"
)

// reportsLocation returns an in-memory location holding a few files.
func reportsLocation() vfs.Location {
	loc, err := mem.NewFileSystem().NewLocation("", "/reports/")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"2026-01.csv", "2026-02.csv", "2026-03.csv", "summary.txt", "notes.md"} {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write([]byte("data")); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	loc := reportsLocation()

	var cursor vfs.Entry
	for page := 1; ; page++ {
		opts := []options.ListOption{list.Limit(2)}
		if page > 1 {
			opts = append(opts, list.After(cursor))
		}

		n := 0
		for e, err := range list.Entries(ctx, loc, opts...) {
			if err != nil {
				log.Fatal(err)
			}
			fmt.Printf("page %d: %s\n", page, e.RelPath())
			cursor = e
			n++
		}
		if n < 2 {
			break
		}
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
page 1: 2026-01.csv
page 1: 2026-02.csv
page 2: 2026-03.csv
page 2: notes.md
page 3: summary.txt
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="ByModTime"></a>
## func ByModTime

```go
func ByModTime(a, b vfs.Entry) int
```

ByModTime compares entries by their listed ModTime. Entries without metadata have the zero time. It is a comparator for slices.SortFunc and [TopN](<#TopN>); swap the arguments to reverse it.

<a name="ByName"></a>
## func ByName

```go
func ByName(a, b vfs.Entry) int
```

ByName compares entries by Name, then by relative path so that entries with the same name in different directories have a stable order. It is a comparator for slices.SortFunc and [TopN](<#TopN>); swap the arguments to reverse it.

<a name="BySize"></a>
## func BySize

```go
func BySize(a, b vfs.Entry) int
```

BySize compares entries by their listed Size. Entries without metadata \(see vfs.Entry.HasMetadata\) have size 0. It is a comparator for slices.SortFunc and [TopN](<#TopN>); swap the arguments to reverse it.

<a name="Collect"></a>
## func Collect

```go
func Collect(seq iter.Seq2[vfs.Entry, error]) ([]vfs.Entry, error)
```

Collect returns every entry seq yields, in order. It stops at the first error and returns it with no entries, so a caller that wants the entries a failed listing did produce, such as for an access report, ranges over the sequence instead. Collect holds the whole listing in memory.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Collect gathers a listing into a slice, stopping at the first error.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/mem"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
)

// reportsLocation returns an in-memory location holding a few files.
func reportsLocation() vfs.Location {
	loc, err := mem.NewFileSystem().NewLocation("", "/reports/")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"2026-01.csv", "2026-02.csv", "2026-03.csv", "summary.txt", "notes.md"} {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write([]byte("data")); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	loc := reportsLocation()

	entries, err := list.Collect(list.Entries(ctx, loc, list.Prefix("2026-"), list.Limit(2)))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		fmt.Println(e.Name())
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
2026-01.csv
2026-02.csv
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="DirFilter"></a>
## func DirFilter

```go
func DirFilter(fn func(e vfs.Entry) bool) options.ListOption
```

DirFilter prunes descent in a recursive listing: nothing beneath a directory for which fn returns false is yielded. The directory itself is still yielded, subject to the other options. To stat an entry or to report a failure from the callback, use [DirFilterContext](<#DirFilterContext>).

<a name="DirFilterContext"></a>
## func DirFilterContext

```go
func DirFilterContext(fn EntryFunc) options.ListOption
```

DirFilterContext is [DirFilter](<#DirFilter>) with a callback that receives the listing's context and can fail. An error from fn ends the listing and is never treated as the directory being pruned.

<a name="DirsOnly"></a>
## func DirsOnly

```go
func DirsOnly() options.ListOption
```

DirsOnly restricts the listing to directories. DirsOnly cannot be combined with [FilesOnly](<#FilesOnly>).

<a name="Entries"></a>
## func Entries

```go
func Entries(ctx context.Context, loc vfs.Location, opts ...options.ListOption) iter.Seq2[vfs.Entry, error]
```

Entries lists the contents of loc as a stream of entries in ascending byte order of [OrderKey](<#OrderKey>), fetching from the backend as the caller iterates. The location itself is never yielded, and a location that does not exist yields nothing. Calling Entries performs no I/O; the listing starts when the returned sequence is ranged over.

```
for e, err := range list.Entries(ctx, loc, list.Recursive(), list.FilesOnly()) {
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println(e.RelPath())
}
```

Options are validated first. An invalid option or combination is yielded as one error that matches [ErrInvalidOption](<#ErrInvalidOption>), and no request is made. Each option may be given at most once, so a caller that adds default options of its own must not repeat them.

If loc implements vfs.EntryLister the backend lists natively and every option is applied again to what it yields, so a backend that ignores an option as a hint is still correct. A callback given to [DirFilter](<#DirFilter>) or [DirFilterContext](<#DirFilterContext>) may therefore be called more than once for the same directory, once by the backend and once here, and should be cheap and free of side effects.

Otherwise Entries falls back to the location's List and ListByPrefix methods. That path yields files only, in byte order, without size or modification time \(see vfs.Entry.HasMetadata\), and it reports [errors.ErrUnsupported](<https://pkg.go.dev/errors/#ErrUnsupported>) for options that need directories: [Recursive](<#Recursive>), [MaxDepth](<#MaxDepth>) and [DirsOnly](<#DirsOnly>), and a [Glob](<#Glob>) containing "/". [DirFilter](<#DirFilter>) and [DirFilterContext](<#DirFilterContext>) only matter to recursive listings, so they have no effect there. A location that does not exist yields nothing; on this path that relies on the location's List returning an error that matches fs.ErrNotExist. Because those methods accept no context, cancellation on the fallback path takes effect only between yielded entries.

Errors are \*fs.PathError values with Op "list". An error yielded with a zero vfs.Entry ends the listing, except one that matches fs.ErrInvalid, which reports a key that cannot be an entry and is followed by the rest of the listing. An error yielded with a directory's entry reports that directory could not be read; the listing continues with the next entry outside it, unless the connection failed, which ends the listing. Errors are never hidden by filters, and do not count toward [Limit](<#Limit>).

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Entries streams a location's contents in byte order. A listing never loads more than it needs, so stopping the loop stops the requests.

	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"2026-01.csv", "2026-02.csv", "2026-03.csv", "summary.txt", "notes.md"} {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write([]byte("data")); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	loc := reportsLocation()

	for e, err := range list.Entries(ctx, loc) {
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		fmt.Println(e.RelPath())
	}
}
```

```

2026-02.csv
2026-03.csv
notes.md
summary.txt

<details><summary>Example (Recursive)</summary>
<p>

Recursive and FilesOnly together list every file under a location, however deep.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/mem"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
)

func archiveLocation() vfs.Location {
	loc, err := mem.NewFileSystem().NewLocation("", "/archive/")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	files := []struct {
		path string
		size int
	}{
		{"readme.txt", 10},
		{"2025/q1/sales.csv", 400},
		{"2025/q2/sales.csv", 250},
		{"2026/q1/sales.csv", 900},
		{"2026/q1/notes.md", 30},
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(file.path)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write(make([]byte, file.size)); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()

	for e, err := range list.Entries(ctx, archiveLocation(), list.Recursive(), list.FilesOnly()) {
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		fmt.Println(e.RelPath())
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
2025/q1/sales.csv
2025/q2/sales.csv
2026/q1/notes.md
2026/q1/sales.csv
readme.txt
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="FilesOnly"></a>
## func FilesOnly

```go
func FilesOnly() options.ListOption
```

FilesOnly restricts the listing to files. It does not stop a recursive listing from descending into directories. FilesOnly cannot be combined with [DirsOnly](<#DirsOnly>).

<a name="Filter"></a>
## func Filter

```go
func Filter(fn func(e vfs.Entry) bool) options.ListOption
```

Filter yields only entries for which fn returns true. It does not affect descent. To stat an entry or to report a failure from the callback, use [FilterContext](<#FilterContext>).

<a name="FilterContext"></a>
## func FilterContext

```go
func FilterContext(fn EntryFunc) options.ListOption
```

FilterContext is [Filter](<#Filter>) with a callback that receives the listing's context and can fail. An error from fn ends the listing and is never treated as the entry being filtered out.

<a name="FlatKeys"></a>
## func FlatKeys

```go
func FlatKeys(ctx context.Context, parent vfs.Location, q Query, pages PageFunc, retry RetryFunc) iter.Seq2[vfs.Entry, error]
```

FlatKeys lists a flat key space, such as an object store, from sorted pages of keys. It is the engine behind the native listing of s3, gs, azure and sqlfs.

Keys that arrive in byte order already are the order every listing guarantees, so nothing is buffered beyond one page. Directories are synthesized from the "/" separators of keys, once each, whether or not a folder marker exists, at the position of their order key. A key that is out of order ends the listing with an error, since a backend whose order differs from byte order would otherwise return silently wrong results. FlatKeys applies q.Prefix, q.StartAfter, q.Depth and, in a recursive listing, q.Descend itself, whatever the backend did with the hints. It does not apply Kind, Glob, Match, Filter or Limit; list.Entries does.

A key that cannot be an Entry, such as "a//b", is yielded as a zero Entry with an error matching fs.ErrInvalid and the listing continues. A failed page ends the listing with an error and a zero Entry, except that a location that does not exist yields nothing. Each page request is wrapped in retry, which may be nil, and is not attempted once ctx is done.

<a name="Glob"></a>
## func Glob

```go
func Glob(pattern string) options.ListOption
```

Glob yields only entries whose relative path matches pattern, at the depth the pattern names: "\*/data.csv" matches "x/data.csv" but not "x/y/data.csv". Each "/"\-separated segment of the pattern is matched against the same segment of the path under path.Match rules, so no wildcard or character class, such as "\[^x\]", matches a "/". The pattern must be a relative path with no empty, "." or ".." segments. Glob cannot be combined with [Prefix](<#Prefix>), [Recursive](<#Recursive>) or [MaxDepth](<#MaxDepth>), because it implies them.

Patterns follow path.Match, which differs from POSIX shell globs in two ways worth knowing: a character class such as "\[\[:alpha:\]\]" has no named classes and is read as a set of literal characters, and an inverted range such as "\[b\-a\]" is not an error and matches nothing. "\*\*" is not supported and behaves as "\*".

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Glob selects entries by pattern, using the same rules as path.Match and io/fs.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/mem"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
)

// reportsLocation returns an in-memory location holding a few files.
func reportsLocation() vfs.Location {
	loc, err := mem.NewFileSystem().NewLocation("", "/reports/")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"2026-01.csv", "2026-02.csv", "2026-03.csv", "summary.txt", "notes.md"} {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write([]byte("data")); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	loc := reportsLocation()

	for e, err := range list.Entries(ctx, loc, list.Glob("2026-0[12].csv")) {
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		fmt.Println(e.RelPath())
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
2026-01.csv
2026-02.csv
```

</p>

<a name="Limit"></a>
## func Limit

```go
func Limit(n int) options.ListOption
```

Limit ends the listing after n entries have been yielded. Errors do not count toward the limit. n must be at least 1.

<a name="Match"></a>
## func Match

```go
func Match(re *regexp.Regexp) options.ListOption
```

Match yields only entries whose relative path matches re. It does not affect descent.

<a name="MaxDepth"></a>
## func MaxDepth

```go
func MaxDepth(n int) options.ListOption
```

MaxDepth stops descent so that no entry deeper than n path segments below the location is yielded. n must be at least 1, and MaxDepth requires [Recursive](<#Recursive>). MaxDepth cannot be combined with [Glob](<#Glob>).

<a name="OrderKey"></a>
## func OrderKey

```go
func OrderKey(e vfs.Entry) string
```

OrderKey returns the key entries are ordered by: the entry's relative path, with "/" appended for directories. Because "\-" sorts before "/", the file "logs\-2024.gz" is listed before the directory "logs". Byte order of the key equals the order object stores return full keys in, which is what lets them stream a listing without buffering.

<a name="Prefix"></a>
## func Prefix

```go
func Prefix(p string) options.ListOption
```

Prefix restricts the listing to entries whose relative path starts with p. A prefix containing "/" is relative to the listed location, so Prefix\("to/rep"\) matches "to/report.csv". An empty p is the same as omitting the option. Prefix cannot be combined with [Glob](<#Glob>).

<a name="Recursive"></a>
## func Recursive

```go
func Recursive() options.ListOption
```

Recursive lists every file and directory beneath the location instead of only its immediate children.

<a name="StartAfter"></a>
## func StartAfter

```go
func StartAfter(relPath string) options.ListOption
```

StartAfter yields only entries whose order key \(see [OrderKey](<#OrderKey>)\) sorts after relPath. A trailing "/" on relPath denotes a directory. An empty relPath is the same as omitting the option, so a paging loop can pass its cursor unconditionally. StartAfter cannot be combined with [After](<#After>).

<a name="TopN"></a>
## func TopN

```go
func TopN(seq iter.Seq2[vfs.Entry, error], n int, compare func(a, b vfs.Entry) int) ([]vfs.Entry, error)
```

TopN returns the n entries of seq that sort first under compare, in that order, keeping only n entries in memory however long the listing is. Entries that compare equal keep the order in which seq yielded them. To find the largest files, pass a comparator that sorts larger sizes first, such as one that swaps the arguments of [BySize](<#BySize>). TopN stops at the first error and returns it with no entries. It returns an error matching [ErrInvalidOption](<#ErrInvalidOption>) if n is below 1 or compare is nil, without ranging over seq.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

TopN keeps only the best n entries, so finding the largest files uses memory for n entries however many are listed.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/mem"
	"github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/list"
)

func archiveLocation() vfs.Location {
	loc, err := mem.NewFileSystem().NewLocation("", "/archive/")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	files := []struct {
		path string
		size int
	}{
		{"readme.txt", 10},
		{"2025/q1/sales.csv", 400},
		{"2025/q2/sales.csv", 250},
		{"2026/q1/sales.csv", 900},
		{"2026/q1/notes.md", 30},
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		f, err := loc.NewFile(file.path)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if _, err := f.Write(make([]byte, file.size)); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return loc
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()

	largestFirst := func(a, b vfs.Entry) int { return list.BySize(b, a) }
	largest, err := list.TopN(list.Entries(ctx, archiveLocation(), list.Recursive(), list.FilesOnly()), 2, largestFirst)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, e := range largest {
		fmt.Println(e.RelPath(), e.Size())
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
2026/q1/sales.csv 900
2025/q1/sales.csv 400
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="WalkDirs"></a>
## func WalkDirs

```go
func WalkDirs(ctx context.Context, parent vfs.Location, q Query, readDir ReadDirFunc, retry RetryFunc) iter.Seq2[vfs.Entry, error]
```

WalkDirs lists a hierarchical backend, one directory read at a time. It is the engine behind the native listing of backends that read a directory per request, such as os, sftp and ftp.

Each directory's children are sorted by order key and walked depth first, which yields the byte order of full paths that every listing guarantees. Descent stops at q.Depth, skips directories outside q.Prefix and subtrees that sort entirely before q.StartAfter, and honors q.Descend in a recursive listing, calling it for each directory about to be read. WalkDirs does not apply Kind, Glob, Match, Filter or Limit; list.Entries does.

If reading the location itself fails the error is yielded with a zero Entry and the listing ends, except that a location which does not exist yields nothing. If reading a subdirectory fails, the error is yielded together with that directory's Entry and the walk continues with the next entry outside it, unless the failure is of the connection itself \(a closed or reset connection, an unexpected end of file, a network or name resolution error\), which would fail every remaining directory the same way: that error is yielded with a zero Entry and the listing ends. A child with an invalid name is yielded as a zero Entry with an error matching fs.ErrInvalid, before the valid entries of its directory, and the walk continues.

Each read is wrapped in retry, which may be nil, and is not attempted once ctx is done. No read is in progress while the caller's loop body runs, and none is started after the caller stops iterating.

<a name="Child"></a>
## type Child

Child describes one child of a directory, as a hierarchical backend reads it.

```go
type Child struct {
    // Name is the child's base name. A name that cannot be part of an Entry's path is reported as a non-fatal error
    // matching fs.ErrInvalid, not as an entry.
    Name string
    // IsDir reports whether the child is a directory. A symbolic link is not a directory here, even if it points to
    // one, so listings never follow links; report it with vfs.WithEntryMode(fs.ModeSymlink | perm).
    IsDir bool
    // Options supply the listed size and modification time, mode and native object.
    Options []vfs.EntryOption
}
```

<a name="EntryFunc"></a>
## type EntryFunc

EntryFunc decides whether an entry passes a filter. It receives the context of the listing, so a callback can call vfs.Entry.InfoContext, and it can fail. A non\-nil error ends the listing.

```go
type EntryFunc func(ctx context.Context, e vfs.Entry) (bool, error)
```

<a name="Kind"></a>
## type Kind

Kind restricts which kind of entry a listing yields.

```go
type Kind int
```

<a name="KindAny"></a>

```go
const (
    // KindAny yields files and directories.
    KindAny Kind = iota
    // KindFiles yields files only.
    KindFiles
    // KindDirs yields directories only.
    KindDirs
)
```

<a name="Object"></a>
## type Object

Object is one key of a flat key space, as an object store lists it.

```go
type Object struct {
    // Key is the object's key relative to the listed location, with no leading slash. A key ending in "/" is a folder
    // marker and is folded into the directory it names. The empty key, the location's own marker, is ignored.
    Key string
    // Options supply the listed size and modification time, mode and native object. They are ignored for markers,
    // because directories never carry metadata.
    Options []vfs.EntryOption
}
```

<a name="Page"></a>
## type Page

Page is one page of a flat listing.

```go
type Page struct {
    // Objects are the keys of the page, in ascending byte order.
    Objects []Object
    // Prefixes are the rolled-up directories of a delimited page, each ending in "/", in ascending byte order.
    Prefixes []string
    // Done reports that no page follows.
    Done bool
}
```

<a name="PageFunc"></a>
## type PageFunc

PageFunc fetches the page described by req. FlatKeys calls it sequentially, never while the caller's loop body runs, and not again once the caller stops iterating. A location that does not exist is reported on the first call with an error matching fs.ErrNotExist.

```go
type PageFunc func(ctx context.Context, req PageRequest) (Page, error)
```

<a name="PageRequest"></a>
## type PageRequest

PageRequest describes the page FlatKeys needs next.

```go
type PageRequest struct {
    // StartAfter is the key after which the page must start. A backend that keeps its own continuation token between
    // calls may follow the token instead, because FlatKeys always resumes immediately after the previous page.
    StartAfter string
    // Prefix is the relative path every wanted key starts with, or "".
    Prefix string
    // Delimited reports whether to roll keys up at the next "/" after Prefix and return the rolled-up directories as
    // Page.Prefixes. It is true for a non-recursive listing and false for a recursive one.
    Delimited bool
}
```

<a name="Query"></a>
## type Query

Query is the validated form of a set of listing options. It is what a backend's native listing starts from.

Prefix, Recursive, MaxDepth, Kind, StartAfter, Limit and Descend are hints: a backend may use them to avoid fetching entries that would be discarded, and may ignore any of them, because the listing applies every option to the entries a backend yields. The shared engines, WalkDirs and FlatKeys, apply Prefix, Recursive, MaxDepth, StartAfter and Descend themselves. Glob, Match and Filter are always applied by the listing itself; a backend never needs to evaluate them. When Glob is set, Prefix, Recursive and MaxDepth hold the values the pattern implies.

```go
type Query struct {
    // Prefix is the relative path every yielded entry must start with, or "".
    Prefix string
    // Recursive reports whether entries deeper than Depth's non-recursive limit are listed.
    Recursive bool
    // MaxDepth is the deepest path segment count to list, measured from the listed location, or 0 for no limit. It is
    // only non-zero when Recursive is true.
    MaxDepth int
    // Kind restricts the kind of entry yielded.
    Kind Kind
    // StartAfter is the order key (see OrderKey) after which entries are yielded, or "".
    StartAfter string
    // Limit is the number of entries after which the listing ends, or 0 for no limit.
    Limit int
    // Glob is the path.Match pattern entries' relative paths must match, or "".
    Glob string
    // Match is the expression entries' relative paths must match, or nil.
    Match *regexp.Regexp
    // Filter is the custom filter entries must pass, or nil.
    Filter EntryFunc
    // Descend decides whether to descend into a directory in a recursive listing, or is nil to descend into all. It has
    // no effect on a listing that is not recursive.
    Descend EntryFunc
}
```

<a name="ParseQuery"></a>
### func ParseQuery

```go
func ParseQuery(opts []options.ListOption) (Query, error)
```

ParseQuery validates opts and returns the Query they describe. Any error matches [ErrInvalidOption](<#ErrInvalidOption>).

Each option may be given at most once; [After](<#After>) and [StartAfter](<#StartAfter>) count as one option, as do [Filter](<#Filter>) and [FilterContext](<#FilterContext>), and [DirFilter](<#DirFilter>) and [DirFilterContext](<#DirFilterContext>). Options this package does not define are ignored, so backend\-specific options can be passed alongside.

<a name="Query.Depth"></a>
### func \(Query\) Depth

```go
func (q Query) Depth() int
```

Depth returns the largest depth of entry the listing can yield, or 0 when there is no limit. Depth is the number of segments in an entry's relative path and is always measured from the listed location, so "a/b/c.txt" has depth 3.

A recursive listing is limited only by MaxDepth. A non\-recursive listing is limited to one level inside the directory Prefix names: with no Prefix that is 1 \(immediate children\), and with Prefix "to/rep" it is 2, because the entries of "to" are listed. Backends and engines use Depth rather than re\-deriving this, so that every backend applies the same limit.

<a name="ReadDirFunc"></a>
## type ReadDirFunc

ReadDirFunc reads the children of the directory at relDir, a slash\-separated path relative to the listed location \("" for the location itself\), in any order. A directory that does not exist is reported with an error matching fs.ErrNotExist, and one that cannot be read with fs.ErrPermission when the cause is known.

```go
type ReadDirFunc func(ctx context.Context, relDir string) ([]Child, error)
```

<a name="RetryFunc"></a>
## type RetryFunc

RetryFunc wraps one backend request in the file system's retry policy. A vfs.Retry value, such as the one a file system's Retry method returns, is a RetryFunc. A nil RetryFunc runs each request once.

```go
type RetryFunc = func(wrapped func() error) error
```
